question: What immediate actions must be taken in the event of a man overboard?
gold_answer: Inform the OOW and Master; revert to manual steering and keep the propeller clear of the side the person went over; release the MOB marker and SART on that side; press the Man-Overboard/Mark-Position button on the GPS and ECDIS; sound the MOB signal (three prolonged blasts); sound the General Emergency Alarm and inform crew over the PA; reduce speed and commence a Williamson turn; post additional lookouts (search lights at night); inform the Engineer of the Watch and place engines on standby — do NOT use the main-engine emergency stop; manoeuvre to rescue or search per IAMSAR; hoist signal flag 'O'; prepare the rescue boat and equipment; distribute portable VHF radios; rig pilot ladder/nets or lower a survival-suit crew member; create a lee when approaching; handle hypothermia; hoist a recovered person in a seated (deck-chair) position to avoid suspension trauma; coordinate with third parties; recover the MOB marker/SART; record all actions in the Log Book; preserve the VDR; switch off Wi-Fi and crew internet (Social Media Policy); conduct alcohol tests (and drug tests if the incident is Severity Level 3+).

citations.quote: Inform the Officer of the Watch and Master ... commence Williamson turn ... place the engines on standby ... Hoist signal flag ... Switch off Wi-Fi and crew internet

question: What is the procedure for a seafarer to raise and escalate a grievance?
gold_answer: (1) Address the complaint to the Head of Department or the seafarer's superior officer. (2) The HOD/superior officer attempts to resolve it as soon as the ship's service permits — preferably within a time limit not exceeding 5 days. (3) If unresolved to the seafarer's satisfaction, refer it to the Master, who handles it personally. (4) The seafarer always has the right to be accompanied and represented by another seafarer of their choice. (5) Complaints and decisions are recorded onboard, with a copy given to the seafarer. (6) If not satisfied with the Master's action (or inaction), the seafarer may state their dissatisfaction and lodge a complaint to the Crewing Manager. (7) Once received ashore, the complaint must be resolved within 8 days. (8) If the complaint is against the Master, the seafarer is encouraged to approach the DPA/Crewing Manager. (9) The seafarer always retains the right to file complaints directly with the Master, vessel owner and competent authorities. (10) The complainant's rights are protected and not prejudiced by making the complaint.

citations.quote: All complaints should be addressed to the Head of the Department ... preferably within a time limit not exceeding 5 days ... may refer it to the master ... wishes to lodge a complaint to the Crewing Manager ... resolved within 8 days ... the complaint is against the Master, the employee is encouraged to approach the DPA/Crewing Manager ... right to be accompanied

question: What is the procedure for breaking the seal and opening the OWS overboard discharge valve?
gold_answer: Keep the OWS overboard valve shut, sealed and locked except when in use — the Master holds the key and the Chief Engineer draws it out only when needed. Break the seal and unlock the overboard discharge valve only after testing the OCM/Whitebox/Greenbox and 3-way valve in recirculation mode AND receiving permission from the bridge/wheelhouse. Record the serial number of the broken seal in the Chief Engineer's Seal Logbook and the Oil Record Book (ORB) as an 'I' coded item. After discharge, lock the overboard valve, install a new seal and return the key to the Master; record the new seal's serial number in the Seal Logbook and ORB as an 'I' coded item and make an appropriate ORB entry for the OWS overboard operation.
